newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi sets deadline for tobacco industry.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi sets deadline for tobacco industry.

text.p: Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore said Wednesday that the tobacco industry had until 3 p.m. EDT (1900 GMT) Thursday to settle the state's landmark lawsuit against cigarette makers or face trial next week.
The state attorney general's office scheduled a news conference for Thursday afternoon to announce the outcome of negotiations with tobacco industry attorneys.
"I will either announce that we're going to trial, or announce that we've settled. I don't know which it will be," Moore said in a telephone interview with Reuters late Wednesday.
Mississippi is one of 40 states which are suing the tobacco industry to recoup state tax dollars spent in recent decades to treat Medicaid recipients for smoking-related illnesses.

The states announced a $368.5 billion national settlement with the industry June 20. But individual states have pressed ahead with their own cases pending settlement approval by the Clinton administration and Congress.

Mississippi hopes to get $1 billion in damages from its lawsuit, which paved the way for other states to lodge similar litigation against cigarette makers. Trial proceedings were scheduled to begin July 9 after two days of preliminary hearings in Jackson County Chancery Court in Pascagoula, Miss.
